Stopper the flask hermetically and leave it for 2 h in the incubator (6.4) at 38 "C. NOTE hydrocyanic test. 6.5 Steam distillation apparatus, provided with a 1 I fiask with ground neck. It should be possible to stopper this removable flask hermetically with a ground stopper. The end of the condenser shall be provided with an extension drawn out to a point. 6.6 ice-water bath.

Cool the flask and its contents in the ice-water bath (6.6). Add 80 ml of water, IO ml of the sodium acetate solution (5.2) and a drop of anti-foaming agent. Fit the flask immediately to the distillation apparatus (6.5).

PROCEDURE

For back titration : 6.9 Volumetric flasks, 250 ml and 500 ml.

Transfer the test portion (8.2) to the 1 I flask (6.5) and add 50 ml of distilled water and IO ml of the sodium acetate solution (5.2) or potassium dihydrogen phosphate solution (5.1). Stopper hermetically, mix well and leave the flask for 12 h in the incubator (6.4) at 38 "C. Cool the flask and its contents by immersion in the ice-water bath (6.6) and add 80 ml of water and a drop of anti-foaming agent; fit the flask to the distillation apparatus (6.5) immediately.

SAMPLING 8.3.2 Distillation 100 ml of distillate.

Prepare a final lot sample of appropriate size in accordance with ISO/R 951 or IS0 2170.

Distil, collecting approximately

8 8.1

PROCEDURE Preparation of test sample

If the direct method of titration (8.3.3.1) in the presence of potassium iodide (5.6) is to be used, collect the distillate in 20 ml of distilled water containing 1 y of sodium hydroxide (5.3). (Solution A.) If the back titration method (8.3.3.2) with the ammcnium thiocyanate solution (5,9) is to be used, collect the distillate in a volume (20 to 50 ml) of the 0,02 N silver nitrate solution (5.8), to which has been added 1 ml of the nitric acid (5.7). (Solution EL) The volume of silver nitrate solution used depends on the presumed content of hydrocyanic acid.

Grind about one-twentieth of the laboratory sample in the previously well-cleaned mechanical grinding mill (6.1). in order to complete the cleaning of the mill, and reject these grindings. Then grind the rest to particles which will pass through the sieve 16.2) completely, collect the grindings, mix thoroughly and carry out the determination without delay. In the case of ground pulses, use the final lot sample. 8.2 Test portion 20 g of the test

8.3.3 8.3.3.1

Weigh, to the nearest 0.1 g, approximately sample (8.1). 8.3 8.3.1 Determination Methods of hydrolysis

Transfer solution A to a 250 ml volumetric flask (6.7), dilute to the mark with distilled wster and mix thoroughly. Pipette 100 ml into a beaker. Add 2 ml of the potassum iodide solution (5.6) anti 1 ml of the ammonia solution (5.4). Titrate with the U,Ol N silver nitrate solution (5.5) until permanent turbidity appears. F3r the easy recognition of the end point of the titration, it IS n?commended that a black background'be u?ed. Make a second titration with another 100 ml portion of distillate and take the mean of the two titrations.

Either of the two alternative procedures which (8.3.1.1 or 8.3.1.2) may be used.

NOTE (to 9.1 and 9.21 - If the standard volumetric solutions used are not of exactly the strength Indicated in the list of reagents, a suitable correction factor should be used in calculating the results.

Test for sulphides

9.3 Take as the result the arithmetic determinations. Express the result to one decimal place.

mean of the two

A nearly black precipitate denotes the presence of a significant quantrty of sulphides, whereas a brownish precipitate denotes only a very slight sulphide content (see clause IO). 8.5 Blank test

NOTE - If the result obtained is less than 10 mg of hydrocyanic acid per kilogram of sample, consider the sample practically free from glycosidic hydrocyanic acid.

Carry out a blank test under the same conditions as in the determination proper but replacing the distillate by distilled water.

10

NOTE ON PROCEDURE

9 9.1

EXPRESSION Direct titration

OF RESULTS

If the distillate contains sulphides or sulphur compounds, a more or less abundant black precipitate appears through action on silver ions. In this case it is advisable to repeat the procedure using only the direct titration method (8.3.3.1), modified by replacing the first paragraph by the following : Transfer the distillate to a 250 ml volumetric flask (6.71, dilute to the mark and mix thoroughly. Pipette 100 ml into a beaker. Add 5 ml of lead nitrate solution (5 g/l) and mix. After allowing to stand for 15 min, filter and wash the beaker, the precipitate and the filter three times, using 10 ml of water each time. Add to the filtrate and washings 2 ml of the potassium iodide solution (5.6) and 1 ml of the ammonia solution (5.4).

ANNEX DETERMINATION OF GLYCOSIDIC HYDROCYANIC ACID BY THE MERCURIMETRIC METHOD

A.0

INTRODUCTION

if the distillate does not contain sulphides or sulphur compounds, the content of glycosidic hydrocyanic acid in pulses can also be determined by back titration with a solution of mercury(ll) nitrate. For this purpose it is convenient to apply the method described in this International Standard, with the following modifications to the clauses and sub-c!auses mentioned below.

mercury(ll) nitrate solution (A.2). to which has been added 1 ml of nitric acid (5.7). (Solution B.) The volume of mercury(l I) nitrate solution used depends on the presumed content of hydrocyanic acid."
